jobs.description:
**About Advanced Energy United**  

Advanced Energy United is a national industry association representing businesses that provide the full range of advanced energy and transportation solutions. Our team works to educate, advocate, and activate in decisionmaker venues across the country.  

We advocate for public policies that enable competition and work alongside our member companies to create economic opportunity, lower consumer costs, and bolster energy reliability and resilience across the country. We work with decision makers at every level of government as well as regulators of energy markets to build progress toward an economy built on advanced energy.  

If you’re an entrepreneurial, innovative, analytical and thoughtful person looking to make an impact in the clean energy space, United might be the perfect place for you to share your talents. Team members at United are given the trust and responsibility to make big things happen, and myriad opportunities to learn new skills, explore new issue areas, and work with a broad cross section of the clean energy community. Being a team member at United also means working with a talented and diverse group of people, some who bring decades of experience spanning advocacy, philanthropy, clean tech, government and more—and our collaborative approach means we get to learn from each other, expert and novice, every day. And while our organization is fully remote, we are proud of the people\-focused culture we have built and the connectedness of our team.  

We work on serious issues, take our mission seriously, but never take ourselves too seriously. **Position Description**  

Advanced Energy United seeks a solutions\-oriented, innovative, and politically savvy Managing Director to join United’s policy team. The Managing Director will oversee a team of advocates and shape policy advocacy strategies in the Central U.S. region, lead member engagement in the region, and work collaboratively with program directors to develop and implement multi\-year strategies and campaigns designed to achieve policy successes that will accelerate the transition to 100% clean energy and electrified transportation while expanding markets for the advanced energy industry.  

This is a unique opportunity to join a high\-functioning team and organization, and lead strategy and execution in key states. The ideal candidate will be a highly energetic and self\-starting professional who brings a background in issue advocacy at the state or federal level and experience with clean energy. The Managing Director will work collaboratively with United’s other Managing Directors, and will lead strategy development and execution, with project teams on both internal and external projects to advance United’s policy agenda in priority states including Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Texas and Wisconsin. Candidates should be creative and flexible, with the ability to develop and execute strategies, working in multiple venues with diverse stakeholders. The successful candidate will have excellent organizational, managerial and mentoring skills, the ability to find common ground both with corporate membership and external stakeholders, and a successful track record generating revenue. Candidates will need to travel frequently to meet with United members, coalition allies and stakeholders, public officials, and internal team members.

 **Responsibilities**  

* Lead development of political and policy strategies for accelerating the transition to 100% clean energy and electrified transportation, as well as identify future venues for policy and political success in targeted states.
* Manage a geographically dispersed advocacy team and lobbyists on the ground.
* Work collaboratively across United’s policy team on developing and implementing strategies to meet short and long\-term policy objectives in key states as part of United’s core portfolio. This will include legislative, regulatory, and administrative (e.g. governor’s office) engagement.
* Work with United members to develop and reach consensus on policy positions in key states and on key issues. Facilitate member calls and lead policy discussions to coalesce member input and prioritize areas of interest and engagement.
* Work with team members to ensure high\-quality member engagement opportunities are conducted in targeted states through direct decision maker engagement, including lobby days and candidate education, earned media, and expert testimony; and participate in legislative, rulemaking, and administrative processes, as needed.
* Develop and maintain excellent working relationships with coalition partners, philanthropy, allies, and key legislative, regulatory and administrative staff.
* Represent United effectively in front of funders and member prospects and help raise funds to support strategies and engagement in key states.
* Ability to master the politics of the region through development of relationships with key players and decision makers, as well as a general understanding of the levers of power in these states and how to leverage the advanced energy industry to affect policy change.
* Travel on an as needed basis (up to 30%) to targeted states for advocacy days, conferences, meetings with key allies and stakeholders, staff development, and other efforts on behalf of United.

 **Required Qualifications**  

* Bachelor’s and/or Advanced degree, Political Science, Public Policy, or Economics preferred, or applicable comparable experience
* Minimum of ten years of professional experience in public policy, with a portion of that engagement in the clean energy or transportation sector
* Experience managing a team in a remote environment
* Viewed as a subject matter expert in a specific focus area
* Political campaign or organizing experience, preferably in the clean energy advocacy space
* Entrepreneurial approach, flexible attitude, and ability to operate independently, making decisions consistent with United’s mission/v

jobs.description:
**Overview**  

The Regional Managing Director, Data Center Community is an externally facing leadership role responsible for earning and sustaining trust in a major Microsoft data center community or regional cluster of communities. The role serves as Microsoft’s local community leader, local stakeholder point of contact, and chief spokesperson for the assigned region, representing the company with civic leaders, elected officials, business organizations, education and workforce partners, nonprofits, media, and community stakeholders.

  

This position is designed for a high\-visibility data center environment where local trust, transparent communications, public engagement, and community benefit are central to Microsoft’s long\-term license to operate. The Managing Director leads a regional team that includes a Community Manager and a Communications Manager and works in close partnership with the local data center operations, as well as Microsoft legal, government affairs, philanthropic and communications teams to deliver a coordinated, locally empowered, and campaign\-ready approach.

  

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

 **Role Scope and Leadership Model**

* Lead Microsoft’s regional data center community strategy, including local stakeholder engagement, public narrative, community investment, and trust\-building priorities.
* Serve as the chief local spokesperson for the region, shaping Microsoft’s voice in community forums, public events, local media engagements, business and civic convenings, and high\-stakes community conversations.
* Manage and guide a regional team and budget consisting of a Community Manager and a Communications Manager, setting priorities, aligning execution, and ensuring the team operates as one integrated local function.
* Partner closely with the local data center operations leader to align community engagement, communications, and operational priorities, ensuring Microsoft shows up as a coordinated and accountable neighbor.
* Coordinate with regional and national surge teams when new market entry, permitting, zoning, local controversy, media attention, or urgent community concerns require additional support.
* Manage a locally focused budget to enable local partnerships and support community priorities in relation to the data center and its operations.
 **Responsibilities** **Regional Leadership and Community Strategy**

* Own and accountable for the integrated community engagement strategy for the assigned data center region, translating Microsoft’s public Community\-First AI Infrastructure commitments into locally relevant plans, partnerships, communications, and measurable outcomes.
* Build and sustain trusted relationships with local elected officials, civic leaders, business organizations, education and workforce institutions, nonprofits, labor partners, community advocates, and other priority stakeholders.
* Represent Microsoft as a trusted local leader in public forums, community meetings, advisory boards, chambers of commerce, business councils, nonprofit coalitions, and other high\-impact venues.
* Anticipate community risks and opportunities, maintain a clear stakeholder map, identify emerging sentiment, and escalate issues quickly with recommendations for action.
* Ensure community engagement begins early, remains transparent, and continues through the full data center lifecycle, including planning, construction, operations, expansion, and moments of heightened scrutiny.
 **Chief Spokesperson and Public Narrative**

* Serve as Microsoft’s chief local spokesperson for the assigned data center community, delivering clear, credible, plain\-language messages about Microsoft’s investments, operations, community commitments and impact, and long\-term presence.
* Guide the local narrative across community engagement, media, social sentiment, public meetings, and stakeholder communications, ensuring consistency with Microsoft’s regional and national messaging while remaining responsive to local needs.
* Prepare for and lead public\-facing engagements such as town halls, hearings, office hours, tours, groundbreaking events, listening sessions, briefings, and community benefit discussions.
* Work with the Communications Manager to develop talking points, FAQs, briefings, local proof points, media materials, rapid\-response guidance, and storytelling that demonstrates Microsoft’s accountability and community impact.
* Act as the trusted local voice during sensitive moments, helping Microsoft respond with transparency, empathy, speed, and operational accuracy.
 **Communications and Community Engagement Oversight**

* Lead the regional team’s budget communications and community engagement operating rhythm, ensuring the Community Manager and Communications Manager have clear priorities, coordinated plans, and defined accountability.
* Oversee local communications strategy, including proactive storytelling, local media engagement, social sentiment monitoring, stakeholder updates, community event messaging, and crisis\-response readiness.
* Guide community programming and philanthropic investments, ensuring local grants, sponsorships, employee engagement, AI skilling, workforce initiatives, nonprofit partnerships, and education programs align with community priorities and Microsoft commitments.
* Connect communications, media, and community efforts so local programs generate credible proof points and community voices that strengthen trust and demonstrate tangible benefit.
* Ensure the regional team maintains accurate data, metrics, outcomes, and qualitative feedback to support internal reporting, public transparency,

jobs.title: Day Program - Program Director
jobs.description:
**Company Summary:**  

Beacon is a successful and national behavioral health company providing residential\-based services and supports to children and adults with Intellectual and Developmental Disabilities, Severe Mental Illness, Autism, and high\-acuity behaviors. All activities related to this position must be delivered in compliance with the company’s policies and procedures, accreditation standards, state and federal licensing requirements, HCBS guidelines, and the contractual requirements of Community Mental Health Agencies and other regulatory bodies. You are expected to be aligned with the goals and mission of the organization, and to perform in accordance with our “I CARE” core values of the organization – Integrity, Compassion, Advocacy, Respect and Excellence.
  
  

**Position Summary:**  

The Program Director oversees assigned Beacon locations to ensure that company goals, budgets, and clinical effectiveness targets are met. They support Care Team Managers by ensuring adequate staffing and resources for high\-quality care, and keep department heads informed of staffing, compliance, and operational concerns. The Program Director plans and co\-chairs monthly staff meetings, ensuring that agendas are coordinated, and documentation is filed.
  
They also ensure the consistent application of policies and procedures, monitor Care Team Managers' workload, and review incident reports for timely submission to regulatory agencies. The Program Director communicates with regulatory agencies, assists the compliance department with corrective action plans, and manages Census, payroll costs, and EBITDA targets.
  
Additionally, they ensure accurate time\-and\-attendance reporting, manage staffing needs, and oversee new employee orientation and training compliance. The Program Director addresses personnel issues with HR, Compliance, and Executive Leadership, provides feedback on performance reviews, and manages the DSP leveling program.
  
The Program Director ensures individual protection, personal care, and participation in skill\-building activities, maintains accurate records, and performs ongoing audits of Beacon location(s) operations.
  
  

**Responsibilities/Essential Functions:**  

Integrity
  
* Always be compliant with all company and regulatory policies and procedures.
* Operational Oversight: Ensure that company goals, including budget and clinical effectiveness targets, are met.
* Policy Implementation: Consistently apply and deploy BSLS policies, procedures, and care practices.
* Incident Reports: Review incident reports, submit them for approval, and ensure timely submission to regulatory agencies.
* Work Injury Reports: Ensure work injury reports are entered accurately and in a timely manner if needed.
* Record Maintenance: Ensure records are secure, confidential, up\-to\-date, and accurate for individuals and employees.
* Reporting Requirements: Ensure that reporting requirements are met and monitor various plans and quality.
* Ongoing Audits: Perform ongoing audits of location operations, including routine inspections.
* Cooperates with Beacon Specialized Living, the Department of Human Services (DHS) staff or any other regulatory body during any inspection, investigation or inquiry.


Compassion
  
* Supervision: Support and supervise Care Team Managers to ensure adequate staffing and resources for high\-quality care.
* Personal Care Logs/Daily Documentation: Ensure that logs are completed correctly and in a timely manner.
* EMAR/MAR: Ensure accuracy in medication administration records.
* Individual Protection: Ensure individual protection, personal care, and adherence to clinical actions.
* Skill\-Building Activities: Ensure individuals participate in skill\-building and community activities.
* Individual Interaction: Attend individual functions and maintain regular interaction.
* Individual Assessments: Assist with individual assessments, placement, transfers, and discharges.


Advocacy
  
* Communication: Keep department heads informed of staffing, compliance, and operational concerns; collaborate with leadership.
* Licensing Liaison: Communicate with licensing consultants and external agencies to resolve issues.
* Investigation Response: Lead responses to investigations and facilitate access to requested information.
* Compliance Assistance: Assist the compliance department with responses, correspondence, and corrective action plans (CAPs).
* Personnel Issues: Address personnel issues with HR, Compliance, and Executive Leadership.

jobs.title: Regional Director of Development, Major Gifts
jobs.description:
**Company Description**  

By working at Harvard University, you join a vibrant community that advances Harvard's world\-changing mission in meaningful ways, inspires innovation and collaboration, and builds skills and expertise. We are dedicated to creating a diverse and welcoming environment where everyone can thrive.

**Why join Harvard University Central Administration?**


Harvard University's Central Administration (CADM) is a 5,000\+ employee organization that supports the university's overall excellence by understanding and serving the needs of its schools, students, faculty, staff, alumni, and surrounding communities. Through dynamic and collaborative partnerships, CADM provides high\-quality and efficient services to the schools to help them achieve their goals.


Alumni Affairs and Development is a dedicated team supporting Harvard’s advancement activity through front\-line fundraising, alumni and volunteer engagement, technology, prospect management and research, business process, events, communications, and many other areas.


Our goal is to create an environment of respect that leverages the many talents, perspectives, and experiences of our employees; to deliver the strongest possible results by incorporating diverse perspectives into our daily work; and to make AA\&D a great place to work for everyone. We strive to live our values of respect, inclusion, trust, collaboration, continuous improvement and innovation; and open communication and effective information sharing in our daily interactions and our work.


AA\&D is comprised of the Faculty of Arts and Sciences (FAS) Development, Advancement Communications, Events \& Donor Relations (ACEDR), University Development and Advancement Solutions (UDAS), the Harvard Alumni Association (HAA), and Office of Talent, Administration and Policy (OTAP).

 **Job Description**  

This full\-time, exempt position is a member of the FAS Major Gifts team and reports to the Deputy Director of Development, FAS Major Gifts. The incumbent will be charged with developing and executing sophisticated cultivation and solicitation strategies leading to the realization of six and seven\-figure major gifts from an assigned portfolio of approximately 100\+ alumni and parent prospect households on the West Coast. The Regional Director will partner with colleagues in the Principal Gifts, Major Gifts, Gift Planning, and Harvard College Fund teams, and with volunteers and others throughout AA\&D to encourage major gift level support (beginning at $25,000 annually or in the form of $250,000\+ multi\-year pledges) across the FAS. At maturity, this role will generate $5 million\+ per year.  

  

**Job\-Specific Responsibilities:**

* Manage a targeted portfolio of 100\+ households in the West Coast region.
* Responsible for meeting or exceeding assigned goals, including, but not limited to, goals for prospect visits, solicitations, successful gift closures, and dollars raised. Qualify, cultivate, solicit, and steward a portfolio.
* Acquire a deep understanding of assigned prospects’ philanthropic interests, capacity, and inclination through face\-to\-face and virtual meetings.
* Through the development of thoughtful strategies and intentional prioritization of prospects, ensure revenue goals are met by focusing on upgrading donors and through maintaining an active regional presence.
* Utilize knowledge of prospects’ interests, to develop and execute robust, multi\-step prospect strategies. Strategically leverage academic leadership, faculty, and other members of the Harvard community leading to successful solicitation and closure of six and seven\-figure gifts.
* Adhere to all prospect management processes and policies around contact reports, proposals, stage codes etc. to ensure cross\-departmental transparency and effectiveness.
* Serve as a partner to Harvard College Fund, Gift Planning, Major Gift, and Principal Gift colleagues by identifying new prospects, volunteers, and supporting the goals of elevating unrestricted and flexibly restricted support at FAS.
* Actively seek to improve professional skills, knowledge, and understanding of Harvard by developing relationships with colleagues across campus, attending campus events and activities, and participating in training activities.
* Travel occasionally with senior academic and administrative leaders. Responsible for securing visits for all leaders and for constructing meetings to effectively leverage each leader’s time to advance prospect strategies. Responsible for communicating meeting strategies through written briefings and pre\-visit briefing meetings or calls.
* Work closely with senior fundraising leaders within FAS Development, the University Development Office, and other Harvard Schools to coordinate strategies for prospects with multi\-school affiliations and/or interests. Embrace collaboration with these partners to deepen each prospect’s relationship with the university to maximize giving potential through broad interests.
* Serve as a leader, resource, and mentor for other fundraisers in the organization by leveraging their fundraising experience, as well as their knowledge of FAS content acquired through their prospect work to inform prospect strategies. Will be expected to contribute productively to prospect strategy reviews and trainings.
* The above covers the most significant responsibilities of the position. It does not, however, exclude other duties, the inclusion of which would conform with the level of the position.

 **Qualifications** **Basic Qualifications:**

* Bachelor’s degree required.
* Minimum of 7 years of experience in university fundraising or relevant transferable experience required.
* Ability to travel approximately 35% of working days.
* You will be expected to work certain events/campus activities, such as reunions each Spring, and participate in department retreats that are taking place on campus in Cambridge, MA.

**About ASPIRA of New York**

ASPIRA of New York is a mission\-driven, progressive nonprofit organization founded in 1961 to advance the educational and social development of Puerto Rican, Latino, and other historically underserved communities. Rooted in cultural pride and community commitment, ASPIRA empowers youth through leadership development, academic enrichment, and civic engagement.

While grounded in Latino and Puerto Rican heritage, ASPIRA proudly serves all students—regardless of race, ethnicity, gender, religion, sexual orientation, or socioeconomic status. Our inclusive approach creates equitable access to high\-quality opportunities for New York City youth, with a strong focus on leadership cultivation and educational excellence.

For over six decades, ASPIRA of New York has been a powerful advocate for youth and education, impacting thousands of children, families, schools, and community organizations through transformative, culturally responsive programming across the five boroughs.

**Position Overview: Program Director – Afterschool Programs (SONYC/COMPASS)**

ASPIRA of New York currently operates more than 15 afterschool programs in NYC public schools, reaching nearly 6,000 students—many from low\-to\-moderate income households. These programs are designed to extend learning beyond the school day and close opportunity gaps for youth by providing safe, engaging, and enriching environments.

The **Program Director** will serve as the strategic and operational leader of a school\-based afterschool program under the SONYC or COMPASS initiative. Reporting to the Managing Director, the Program Director will oversee all aspects of program implementation—including staff leadership, youth and family engagement, partner collaboration, fiscal management, compliance, and program quality assurance.

This role is ideal for a results\-driven, equity\-centered leader with a passion for youth development, education, and community empowerment. The successful candidate will be someone who models ASPIRA’s values of cultural pride, service, and excellence, and who leads with vision, empathy, and a deep commitment to educational justice.

**Key Focus Areas:**

* Lead the design and execution of high\-impact afterschool programming that integrates Academic Enrichment, Service Learning, Arts, Physical Education, and Social Emotional Learning.
* Inspire, supervise, and develop a dynamic team of youth development professionals.
* Foster strong partnerships with schools, families, and community stakeholders to ensure alignment and responsiveness to youth needs.
* Drive programmatic outcomes through thoughtful planning, data\-informed decision\-making, and ongoing evaluation.
* Ensure full compliance with Department of Youth and Community Development (DYCD), NYC Department of Education (DOE), and Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) regulations.

**Responsibilities:**

* **Curriculum Alignment \& Enrichment:** Collaborate with school\-day leadership to ensure ASPIRA’s afterschool curriculum complements and reinforces daytime instruction while incorporating youth development principles. Design engaging, age\-appropriate, and culturally responsive programming that supports academic growth, creativity, and personal development.
* **Innovative Program Design \& Leadership:** Lead the development and implementation of high\-quality afterschool curriculum that reflects ASPIRA’s mission and the needs of the school community. Ensure programming provides a safe, supportive, and stimulating environment that encourages curiosity, collaboration, and leadership among students.
* **Holistic Student Development:** Provide and sustain enriching programming that balances academic support with opportunities for physical activity, social\-emotional learning, arts, STEM, civic engagement, and leadership development. Prioritize inclusive, empowering experiences that resonate with students’ identities and lived experiences.
* **Data\-Driven Program Management:** Collect, track, and analyze data related to program attendance, participation, student progress, and outcomes. Use data to make informed decisions, assess program impact, and drive continuous improvement. Maintain proper student\-to\-staff ratios in compliance with NYC Department of Health \& Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) standards.
* **Activity Planning \& Cultural Engagement:** Develop and execute engaging activities that spark student interest and enhance learning beyond the classroom. Organize community\-building experiences such as performances, family nights, special events, service learning projects, and field trips that deepen student connection and broaden exposure.
* **Family \& Community Partnership:** Build trusting relationships with families, caregivers, and community members to support student success and increase engagement. Serve as a key connector between families, the school, and ASPIRA’s broader mission and resources.
* **School \& Stakeholder Collaboration:** Maintain strong, collaborative relationships with the school Principal, teachers, and support staff. Attend regular planning meetings to ensure alignment, responsiveness to student needs, and shared accountability. Foster connections with subcontractors and external partners to enhance program offerings.
* **Staff Leadership \& Development:** Recruit, onboard, train, and supervise a high\-performing afterschool team. Provide ongoing feedback and support through regular staff meetings and one\-on\-one supervision. Create individualized professional development plans that promote growth, engagement, and long\-term retention. Submit bi\-weekly payroll and communicate staffing needs to the Managing Director.
* **Operational Oversight \& Compliance:** Ensure timely and accurate maintenance of all records, including attendance, program schedules, and activity documentation, in compliance with DYCD requirements. Oversee the safe and effective daily operation of the afterschool program.
*

**Job Description**

\*\*\*TO BE CONSIDERED FOR THIS POSITION CANDIDATES MUST BE PERMANENT IN THE TITLE OF ADMINISTRATIVE PUBLIC INFORMATION SPECIALIST. ALL OTHER CANDIDATES WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED\*\*\*.
  

  

The Commission on Human Rights (the “Commission”) is the City agency charged with enforcing the New York City Human Rights Law (“City Human Rights Law”), one of the most expansive civil rights laws in the nation, prohibiting discrimination in housing, employment, and public accommodations. The Commission investigates, litigates, and adjudicates claims of discrimination brought by the public. Where the Commission finds unlawful discrimination, harassment, and retaliation have occurred, it obtains compensation to victims, orders companies to take corrective action, and can assess civil penalties. The Commission also engages in training and education to ensure New Yorkers understand their rights and responsibilities under City Law.
  

  

The Director of Communications reports to the Deputy Commissioner of External Affairs and works to develop and implement the communications and public relations strategy for the agency. The Director of Communications leads a team of communications professionals to advance the agency’s mission and execute strategies that advance awareness of the NYCHRL, the CCHR activities, and human rights issues impacting New Yorkers. The position collaborates with agency stakeholders, media, press, bloggers, advocates, community groups, elected officials and the general public.
  

  

Job Duties
  

* Develop communications and marketing strategies to advance Commission goals.
* Manage the agency’s communication budget.
* Direct all aspects of agency communications and marketing, maintaining consistent strategic visibility for the Commission via broadcast and print media (ethnic and non\-ethnic), social media and other platforms.
* Identify new campaigns to educate New Yorkers about rights and obligations under the Human Rights Law (HRL).
* Develop and build positive relationships with media, elected officials, agency stakeholders and the community.
* Convene focus groups and utilize other research techniques, to inform the development and evaluate the impact of campaign strategies.
* Develop and disseminate multi\-lingual materials to educate New Yorkers about their rights and obligations under the HRL.
* Cultivate and maintain strong relationships with journalists, including ethnic media editors and other contacts as appropriate in print and broadcast media.
* Act as an agency spokesperson and serve as a key contact for media, elected officials, agency stakeholders and the community.
* Ensure the Commission’s message reaches a broad cross\-section of NYC communities through significant ethnic media ad buys.
* Coordinate and collaborate with members of the Mayor’s Office Communications Team, the City Hall Press Office about Commission strategy and incoming stories, as well as with press and communications staff at sister agencies, as appropriate.
* Supervise staff in the Communications Team and support professional development through assignments and training opportunities.
* Lead the completion of reports required under the HRL or Charter through the development and review of content.
* Other duties as assigned.

**About Us**



Kardigan is a heart health company working to make cardiovascular disease preventable, curable and no longer the leading cause of death in the world.  


It is Kardigan's mission to develop multiple targeted treatments in parallel that bring people with cardiovascular diseases to the cures they deserve.

Led by Tassos Gianakakos, Jay Edelberg, M.D., Ph.D., and Bob McDowell, Ph.D., Kardigan's co\-founders have reunited after leading MyoKardia to discover and develop mavacamten, the first cardiac myosin inhibitor, resulting in an acquisition by Bristol Myers Squibb in 2020\.

We have a cutting\-edge discovery and translational research platform, a pipeline of late\-stage candidates, and an industry\-leading team that is driven to improve the lives of patients.

At Kardigan, we are motivated by our values which guide how we work, interact, and achieve our goals. **Driven by patients and their families**, we are deeply committed to improving the lives of patients and prioritizing their needs above all else. We believe in **being authentic**—leading with truth to bring out the best in others by creating an environment where every person knows they will be fully accepted. With an **eagerness to learn**, we encourage the highest levels of curiosity and are open to changing our minds. We are committed to **winning as a team** with urgency, excellence, and intention, and support each other no matter what role we play or where we sit. Lastly, we strive to **enable the impossible** because patients are counting on us. We are not afraid to take risks to unlock innovation and advance scientific discoveries.

These values are the foundation of our work, empowering us to make a real difference, every day. **About the Team**  

Kardigan's Regulatory Affairs team is a collaborative and strategic partner in advancing our portfolio of investigational cardiovascular therapies. Working closely with colleagues across Clinical Development, Medical Affairs, Safety, CMC, Quality and other functions, the team translates evolving science and development plans into clear regulatory strategies that support high\-quality decisions and productive engagement with global health authorities.



We are building a team that combines scientific rigor, sound judgment, and a practical, solutions\-oriented mindset. Team members have the opportunity to shape regulatory approaches, establish scalable ways of working, and influence programs at important stages of development. Our work helps Kardigan move with urgency while maintaining the highest standards of quality, ethics, and compliance, ultimately supporting our mission to bring potentially transformative treatments to people living with cardiovascular disease.


**Job Overview**  

Kardigan is seeking an Executive Director, Regulatory Strategy to lead global regulatory strategy across our portfolio of investigational cardiovascular therapies. Reporting to the SVP, Regulatory Affairs, this leader will serve as the regulatory lead on program teams, own the development and execution of regulatory strategy in line with the integrated development plan for late\-stage clinical programs, and act as the primary interface with the U.S. Food and Drug Administration while directing ex\-US regulatory activities with support from consultants, vendors, and partners.



This is a high\-ownership role in a fast\-paced, entrepreneurial environment. The Executive Director will help define regulatory pathways for investigational therapies, including in indications without established regulatory precedent, and will help build Kardigan's regulatory capabilities, processes, and team as the portfolio matures. Early priorities include refining program regulatory strategies and health authority engagement plans, establishing regulatory risk registers and regulatory intelligence monitoring, contributing to core regulatory processes and infrastructure, and managing the consultants and vendors supporting the portfolio. Significant regulatory strategy decisions and major agency positions will be developed in partnership with, and subject to alignment with, the SVP, Regulatory Affairs and the Executive Leadership Team.

new_jobs.description:
**Help Shape the Future of Recovery Housing in Washington**

The Washington Alliance for Quality Recovery Residences (WAQRR) is seeking an Executive Director who is passionate about building strong organizations, supporting recovery housing providers, and improving outcomes for individuals in recovery.

This is a unique opportunity to lead a respected statewide nonprofit that establishes quality standards for recovery residences, provides technical assistance to operators, and serves as the Washington affiliate for the National Alliance for Recovery Residences (NARR).

The Executive Director works closely with the Board of Directors to provide strategic leadership while also managing day\-to\-day operations of the organization. We’re looking for someone who enjoys building systems, developing relationships, solving problems, and helping mission\-driven organizations thrive.

**What You’ll Do**

No two days look exactly alike, but your work will focus on five key areas.

Lead the Organization

* Partner with the Board of Directors to execute WAQRR’s strategic priorities.
* Develop policies, procedures, and operational systems that support long\-term success.
* Supervise staff and contractors, providing coaching, accountability, and support.
* Prepare board materials, provide organizational updates, and help guide governance activities.

Strengthen Financial Stability

* Develop and manage the annual budget.
* Monitor financial performance and present regular reports to the Board.
* Ensure compliance with financial policies and reporting requirements.
* Pursue grants, contracts, and other funding opportunities that strengthen the organization’s future.

Oversee Accreditation and Quality

* Lead WAQRR’s statewide recovery residence accreditation program.
* Ensure accreditation activities remain aligned with NARR standards.
* Support continuous quality improvement for accredited recovery residences.
* Oversee the grievance review process with the Grievance Review Committee while maintaining fairness, consistency, and appropriate documentation.

Support Recovery Residence Operators

* Provide guidance and technical assistance to operators throughout Washington.
* Help organizations strengthen policies, practices, and compliance.
* Develop educational resources and training opportunities.
* Coordinate conferences, meetings, and other learning events.

Build Partnerships

* Represent WAQRR with state agencies, community partners, and stakeholders.
* Serve as a spokesperson for the organization.
* Build relationships that strengthen recovery housing across Washington.
* Use data to evaluate impact and communicate results to funders, partners, and members.

**What Success Looks Like**

In your first year, you’ll help WAQRR become an even stronger organization by:

* Building trusted relationships with members, partners, and the Board.
* Strengthening operational systems and organizational processes.
* Supporting a high\-quality, consistent, accreditation program.
* Identifying opportunities for sustainable funding and growth.
* Helping recovery residence operators succeed through education and technical assistance.

**What We’re Looking For**

You may be an excellent fit if you:

* Enjoy balancing strategy with hands\-on execution.
* Strengthening operational systems and organizational processes.
* Supporting a high\-quality, consistent accreditation program.
* Identifying opportunities for sustainable funding and growth.
* Helping recovery residence operators succeed through education and technical assistance.

Required Qualifications

* Bachelor’s degree in a human services\-related field or equivalent professional experience.
* Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
* 7\-10 years of progressive senior leadership experience, including experience leading and developing teams.
* Demonstrated experience building, growing, or scaling an organization, program, or initiative.
* Experience managing complex organizational budgets and overseeing public and private grants, contracts, or other funding sources.
* Experience working in advocacy, public policy, legislative affairs, or systems change initiatives.
* Knowledge of behavioral health, mental health, housing, and/or community\-based recovery systems.
* Experience working collaboratively with Boards of Directors, executive leadership, or governing bodies.
* Valid driver’s license and ability to travel throughout Washington.

Preferred Qualifications

* Executive Director or CEO experience.
* Experience in recovery housing or familiarity with NARR standards.
* Experience working with state agencies in Washington.
* Experience using data to communicate organizational impact and influence policy.
* Experience leading remote or geographically dispersed teams.
* Experience working with nonprofit boards.
* Grant writing or nonprofit fundraising experience.
* Experience managing budgets and organizational finances.

To apply, please complete an application here: https://airtable.com/embed/app9MSdIFk8IN4MGD/pagRkGgSRKei0FQFL/form

**Why WAQRR?**

Recovery housing changes lives, and quality matters.

At WAQRR, you’ll have the opportunity to strengthen recovery housing across Washington by supporting providers, building partnerships, and helping ensure people in recovery have access to safe, high\-quality homes where they can thrive.

If you’re looking for meaningful work where your leadership can have a statewide impact, we’d love to hear from you.

*We recognize that strong candidates may not meet every qualification. If you’re excited about this opportunity, we encourage you to apply.*

Pay: $105,000\.00 \- $120,000\.00 per year

Work Location: Hybrid remote in Mount Vernon, WA 98273

**About Green Our Planet**

Green Our Planet is a national nonprofit that teaches people to grow food. We run three programs:

* **Schools** — students grow food in gardens and hydroponic labs, learn science, nutrition, and financial literacy, and sell what they grow at student\-run farmers' markets.
* **Workplaces** — hydroponic gardens in offices and facilities, run as an employee wellness program.
* **Communities** — hydroponic systems and coaching for families, delivered through health, government, and community partners.

We work in 44 states and have more than 1,300 programs running today.

We are growing. The Clark County School District is expanding our programs toward 200 elementary schools, our student farmers markets are moving outside Nevada under a federal USDA award, and Compassionate Gardens, our new Las Vegas headquarters and community hub, is opening.

**About the Role**

The Director of Operations leads the team that delivers our programs in the field. This is a hands\-on leadership role. You will spend a significant part of each week at schools, gardens, and partner sites — watching the work happen, coaching staff in the moment, and making sure every site meets our standard.

We have the systems: a documented customer journey, a CRM, a reporting platform, defined roles, and clear performance measures. What we need is a leader who makes sure the work gets done consistently, everywhere, every week.

This role is designed for a leader who wants to grow into broader organizational leadership over time. Green Our Planet has learned that success here starts with understanding the work firsthand. The right person will spend their first years deeply engaged in day\-to\-day operations, building relationships with staff, customers, schools, and community partners, and developing a thorough understanding of how our programs operate.

As the organization continues to grow, this role has the potential to expand into a broader executive leadership position. Advancement will come through demonstrated results, strong people leadership, operational excellence, and a proven ability to scale programs while staying connected to the work on the ground.

**This is not a role for someone looking to manage from a distance. It is an opportunity for a hands\-on leader who wants to earn the trust, knowledge, and experience necessary to help lead the organization's future.**

* Learn our annual priorities, understand where each one stands, and take ownership of the parts this team delivers.
* Get to know every person on the team, what they are responsible for each week, and how their work is tracking.
* Establish a consistent weekly field schedule so farmers, coaches, and hydroponics staff are at their sites on a predictable rhythm.
* Assess every site against our quality standard and build a plan to close any gaps.
* Close the loop on reporting so every site visit produces an action plan and every action plan gets followed through.
* Set clear performance expectations with each team member and address gaps early, with support from HR.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Team Leadership and Accountability**

* Set clear weekly expectations for each team member and follow up on them.
* Hold regular check\-ins, field observations, and performance conversations.
* Build a culture where standards are clear, measured, and met.

**Field Execution and Customer Experience**

* Own the quality of our customer relationships: schools, districts, workplaces, and community partners.
* Identify customer needs early and reset expectations when scope or capacity changes.
* Visit sites regularly and see the work firsthand.

**Program Quality and Standards**

* Hold every garden and hydroponic system to our quality standard, and inspect against it in person.
* Strengthen the planting, maintenance, and inspection routines that keep sites healthy and productive.
* Escalate and resolve facility and infrastructure issues that get in the team’s way.
* Deliver the grant and sponsorship commitments this team owns, on schedule.

**Systems and Reporting**

* Get the team using our CRM and reporting platform consistently.
* Use reports and dashboards to catch problems early and act on them.
* Improve the systems that get in the team’s way.

**Budget and Risk**

* Manage the team's operating budget
* Keep program spending in line with the grants and sponsorships that fund it, working with our finance and grants staff.

**Planning for Growth**

* Plan staffing, schedules, and routing for a much larger school footprint.
* Partner with the CEO and Senior Director of Finance \& HR on hiring, structure, and budget.
* Support Compassionate Gardens as a working headquarters and program site.

**Qualifications**

**Required**

* Five or more years leading frontline or field\-based teams
* A track record of improving an existing team’s performance: setting expectations, coaching, and following through.
* Demonstrated success leading teams while remaining directly involved in day\-to\-day operations and execution. Candidates should be comfortable balancing strategic thinking with hands\-on problem solving and operational accountability.
* Strong organizational skills and comfort with CRM, project management, and reporting tools.
* Willingness to work in the field on a regular basis, including outdoors and at school sites.
* Valid driver’s license and reliable transportation.

**Preferred**

* Bachelor’s degree in business, operations, education, organizational leadership, or a related field.
* Experience leading other managers.

* Experience with budgets and using data to make decisions.

new_jobs.title: Director of Development
new_jobs.description:
**Join Our Mission to Transform Lives**

At Mend Culture Inc., we believe that meaningful change happens when compassion meets action. As a nonprofit organization committed to cultivating an inclusive community environment, we recognize that our greatest strength lies in our people. Every team member is valued, supported, and empowered to make a genuine difference in the lives of those we serve. If you're passionate about social justice and ready to be part of a team that truly cares about both our community and each other, we'd love to meet you.

**DIRECTOR OF DEVELOPMENT** 

**General Summary of Purpose of this Position:**The Director of Development serves as a key member of the leadership team, reporting directly to the Chief Executive Officer. This position provides high\-level strategic oversight for all fundraising, executive donor relations, board engagement, and development activities. Additionally, the Director champions the organization's mission by directly supporting program operations, including outreach activities, canvassing efforts, and community resource coordination. This is a full\-time position requiring flexible scheduling and occasional evening/weekend availability.

**Specific Duties and Responsibilities:** The statements describe essential functions but are not all\-inclusive. Individuals may perform other duties as assigned. Percentages estimate time spent on each duty.

**Strategic Development Leadership** 

* Develops and implements comprehensive, multi\-year fundraising strategies aligned with the organizational mission.
* Creates annual development plans with specific revenue targets, budgets, and implementation timelines.
* Collaborates closely with the Chief Executive Officer and Board of Directors on organizational fundraising strategy, capital campaigns, and major donor initiatives.
* Analyzes regional and national funding trends to identify new revenue streams and high\-level donor prospects.

**Grant Research and Opportunity Identification** 

* Researches and identifies major grant opportunities from government agencies, national foundations, and corporate funders.
* Oversees the maintenance of a comprehensive grant opportunity database with strict tracking of deadlines and compliance requirements.
* Presents viable grant opportunities to the leadership team with strategic recommendations and ROI analyses.
* Coordinates with program staff and the Associate Director to gather data and narratives needed for complex grant applications.
* Cultivates and maintains institutional relationships with current funders while identifying new funding partnerships.

**Donor Relations and Stewardship** 

* Develops and maintains deep relationships with individual major donors, major gift prospects, and prominent corporate sponsors.
* Conceptualizes and oversees the execution of signature fundraising events, annual campaigns, and high\-level donor appreciation activities.
* Develops annual giving programs, legacy giving initiatives, and specialized donor recognition programs.
* Ensures proper donor acknowledgment frameworks and tax\-compliant gift processing systems are strictly maintained.

**Community Engagement and Partnership Development** 

* Represents Mend Culture Inc. at key community events, networking functions, and fundraising conferences.
* Builds strategic partnerships with civic organizations, faith communities, municipal leaders, and business executives.
* Develops corporate sponsorship programs, workplace giving initiatives, and cause\-marketing partnerships.
* Serves as a primary organizational spokesperson for development\-related initiatives and media opportunities.

**Program Support and Outreach Assistance** 

* Assists with street outreach activities including canvassing operations in assigned zones to stay connected to the grassroots mission.
* Supports encampment engagement efforts and client relationship\-building activities alongside the program team.
* Coordinates donation pickup systems, distribution logistics, and in\-kind donation drives.
* Provides backup support for housing navigation activities during peak periods or staff shortages.

Pay: $58,000\.00 \- $60,000\.00 per year

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Health insurance
* Paid time off
* Vision insurance

Work Location: In person

The position provides strategic leadership for fundraising, donor engagement and stewardship, Foundation Board governance, financial management, external relations, and Foundation operations.

new_jobs.title: Director of Operations
new_jobs.description:
New Bedford Research \& Robotics

**Director of Operations**


New Bedford, MA \| Full time, onsite \| $85,000 to $110,000

**Opportunity**
===============


New Bedford Research \& Robotics (NBRR) is a nonprofit innovation center where advanced technology and creative work happen on a downtown campus. We help entrepreneurs advance new products, run education and workforce programs, and support research. Founders, students, artists, and engineers work in the same rooms and use the same machines.


On any given day you might see a teenager learning industrial robotics, a marine robotics startup testing a vehicle, an artist in residence making a ceramic bowl with a robot, and an engineer refining a new process. Our campus comprises four buildings on “innovation alley” in New Bedford, and will expand from 15,000 to 33,000 square feet this year when we expand our headquarters.


Our home is a legacy site, the old Glaser Glass building, where for many decades people cut and fit glass for this city's cars, houses, and boats. The tools have changed. What happens inside has not: people learning a trade, testing an idea, and finding out whether it works.


This new role is coming at a time of growth at NBRR. We are looking for a person who understands NBRR’s mission and vision, and has the experience and operational leadership skills to scale, balance, and innovate.

**About NBRR**
==============


New Bedford Research \& Robotics’s programs are designed to stand on their own and to make each other better where they overlap:

* Industry R\&D: aerospace, manufacturing, marine tech, architecture and construction, e\-mobility
* Startups in residence: marine robotics, advanced manufacturing, medical, fashion, data, construction
* Research: AI, robotics, design, new materials
* Community: paid internships, a lecture series, artist and designer residencies
* Education and workforce development: marine robotics, industrial robotics, STEAM


NBRR’s staff of engineers, designers, and educators work across all of it, which is how ideas move between a classroom, a startup, and a manufacturer’s research problem.


Today we have seven full\-time staff, two fractional discipline leaders, 20 to 30 interns a year, and a startup membership on track to reach 25 companies in 2027, alongside partner organizations, universities, and schools. Late fall we will open 18,000 square feet of newly fitted out space.

**The Role**
============


This new position will be the senior operating role at NBRR \- focused on orchestrating and systematizing the ecosystem of programs and people that bring our mission to life. Our campus and technology set the stage for NBRR’s team, startups, interns, research partnerships, and community impact. We’re in pursuit of an experienced and vision\-driven person who can maintain balance and contribute to growth across our programs.

**How This Works With the CEO**
===============================


You would report to Mark Parsons, our Founder and CEO. Here is how we see the roles:

* The CEO owns vision and strategy, fundraising, major external relationships, and the board.
* You would own execution and the daily running of the organization: operations, administration, and facilities.
* You would make routine operational, vendor, and personnel decisions within the approved budget.
* You and the CEO will keep a standing cadence to align on priorities, risks, staffing, and what is coming next.
* You would prepare for and present to the Board of Directors at its quarterly meetings.

**Your Areas of Responsibility**
================================

**People and administration**
-----------------------------

* Turn organizational priorities into plans with owners, timelines, and follow\-through.
* Build and manage the operating team, including a site manager, as we grow.
* With the CEO, hold a culture built on clear communication, accountability, collaboration, and honest feedback.
* Support our department leaders in delivering their programs.
* Serve as first line contact to outside HR, finance, IT, and other providers.
* Make sure the way we recruit interns, hire staff, and fill programs reaches the whole community.
* Keep HR practice current with our HR partner: policies, documentation, onboarding, and performance conversations.

**Systems**
-----------

* Build the annual operating calendar, the workflows, and the accountability systems that make follow\-through visible.
* Evolve and maintain the policies and standard operating procedures a growing organization needs, sized to the organization we actually are.
* Own contracts, insurance, risk management, records, and compliance.
* Name capacity problems early and bring the staffing, vendor, or process answer.

**Community and members**
-------------------------

* Own what it feels like to be here. The member experience is the systems plus everything else: how fast someone gets an answer or whether a new member knows five people by their second week.
* Make sure our 20 to 30 interns a year continue to have a home that is well\-run so they can have a genuinely transformative experience here. They contribute to research and operations, and they are part of the work rather than adjacent to it.
* Support relationship building with community members and partner organizations, coordinating with the CEO and our organizational leaders.

**Campus**
----------

* Run the four\-building, 33,000 square foot campus, located next to the downtown cultural district, a $2B deep water port and the new rail station for the train to Boston.
* Set the facility practices that keep the place efficient, safe, secure, clean, well used, and earning revenue.
* Oversee IT, capital equipment, and building systems, along with the service agreements behind them.

**What Success Looks Like in the First Year**
=============================================

* The expansion into NBRR’s new headquarters is successful. The new space opens and settles, the campus absorbs growth

Chief Operating Officer – Multi\-Location Automotive Repair

**PBAS, LLC is seeking a Chief Operating Officer to lead our automotive repair operations across Tennessee.**

We are looking for a steady, people\-focused leader who enjoys building teams, solving problems, and producing measurable results. The right person wants to win but does not need to dominate the room. They are approachable without avoiding accountability, competitive without creating unnecessary pressure, and organized enough to keep multiple locations moving in the same direction.

The COO will oversee our full\-service automotive repair, exhaust, preventive maintenance, fleet, and USPS vehicle operations. This person will work directly with shop managers, service advisors, technicians, administrative employees, vendors, fleet customers, and ownership.

This is not a desk\-only position. The COO must be visible in the shops, understand what employees need to succeed, recognize problems early, and follow through until they are resolved.

**Primary ResponsibilitiesLeadership and Employee Development**

* Build strong relationships with employees throughout the organization.
* Coach shop managers to become capable, confident, and accountable leaders.
* Establish clear performance expectations for managers, service advisors, technicians, and support employees.
* Conduct regular performance reviews and employee\-development conversations.
* Address attendance, communication, conduct, and performance concerns promptly and professionally.

* Identify high\-potential employees and develop future managers and company leaders.
* Create succession plans so individual locations are not dependent on one person.
* Recognize strong performance and provide direct, constructive coaching when improvement is needed.
* Maintain a positive work environment while consistently enforcing company policies and standards.

**ASE Certification and Technical Training**

A major priority of this position will be building a structured ASE certification and technical\-development program.

The COO will:

* Review each technician’s current certifications, skills, and training needs.
* Create individual ASE certification plans with clear goals and timelines.
* Help employees register for ASE testing and obtain appropriate study materials.
* Coordinate training courses, testing schedules, reimbursement, and certification renewals.
* Track certifications, expiration dates, test results, and continuing education.
* Hold employees accountable for completing agreed\-upon certification plans.

* Build relationships with technical schools and industry training organizations.

**Multi\-Location Shop Operations**

* Oversee daily operations and performance across all PBAS Tennessee locations.
* Visit locations regularly and remain accessible to managers and employees.

* Lead regular management meetings with clear action items, responsible parties, and deadlines.

* Prepare offers and coordinate consistent onboarding.
* Establish clear 30\-, 60\-, and 90\-day expectations for new employees.
* Monitor retention, turnover, attendance, compensation, morale, and development needs.
* Conduct stay interviews and exit interviews to identify preventable turnover.
* Ensure hiring decisions support workload, productivity, payroll goals, and future growth.

Aurora FCA — Development Director

**Salary:** $45,000\-$60,000 (depending on experience)  
**Organization:** Fellowship of Christian Athletes – Aurora FCA  
**Location:** Aurora, Colorado  
**Employment:** Full\-Time (Hybrid)  
**Reports To:** Aurora FCA Director  
**Purpose:** Lead the development and fundraising efforts of Aurora FCA so that financial resources, ministry partnerships, and donor relationships are strengthened to expand the Gospel through coaches and athletes.

About Aurora FCA

Aurora FCA exists to see **coaches and athletes transformed by Jesus Christ and empowered to transform the world**. We serve middle and high school students, coaches, churches, volunteers, and families throughout Aurora by using the influence of sport to make disciples who make disciples.

We believe Aurora FCA should **“Be known for making Jesus Known.”**

As Aurora FCA continues to grow, we are looking for a Development Director who can build the financial and relational foundation necessary for that growth.

Position Overview

The Development Director will provide leadership for the fundraising and development strategy of Aurora FCA. This person will cultivate relationships with current and prospective donors, develop church and community partnerships, lead fundraising campaigns, support staff fundraising efforts, and help create a culture where fundraising is viewed not as a necessary evil, but as an **opportunity for people to join in God's work through FCA**.

The Development Director will work closely with the Aurora FCA Director, staff team, board of directors, volunteers, churches, business leaders, and ministry partners.

Key Responsibilities1\. Donor Development \& Relationship Management

* Develop and maintain a portfolio of individual donors and ministry partners.
* Identify, cultivate, solicit, and steward new donors.
* Build meaningful long\-term relationships with major donors and prospective major donors.
* Develop strategies for increasing donor retention and recurring giving.
* Schedule regular donor meetings, calls, visits, and ministry updates.
* Provide personalized communication and stewardship to key donors.
* Help donors understand the ministry impact of their giving.
* Develop strategies for gifts such as donor\-advised funds, stock gifts, major gifts, and legacy giving.

2\. Fundraising Strategy

* Create and execute an annual development plan aligned with Aurora FCA's ministry strategy.
* Establish annual fundraising goals and measurable objectives.
* Lead year\-end, Giving Tuesday, special campaigns, and other fundraising initiatives.
* Develop creative fundraising opportunities for individuals, churches, businesses, and community partners.
* Track progress toward fundraising goals and communicate regularly with leadership and the board.
* Help Aurora FCA develop sustainable revenue rather than relying primarily on one\-time gifts.
* Assist staff members in developing and maintaining their personal ministry support teams when appropriate.

3\. Church \& Community Partnerships

* Develop relationships with pastors, churches, businesses, foundations, and community leaders.
* Create a clear pathway for churches to become active ministry partners with Aurora FCA.
* Identify churches that can provide financial support, volunteers, prayer, facilities, meals, and other resources.
* Develop business and community sponsorship opportunities.
* Help communicate Aurora FCA's vision and ministry opportunities to churches and community organizations.
* Represent Aurora FCA at community and ministry events.

4\. Board Development \& Engagement

* Partner with the board's development/fundraising efforts.
* Equip board members to participate meaningfully in fundraising.
* Provide board members with tools, talking points, donor information, and opportunities to engage prospective supporters.
* Help develop a board culture where every board member is actively involved in advancing the mission.
* Provide regular fundraising reports and updates to the board.

5\. Communications \& Storytelling

* Work with the Aurora FCA team to communicate compelling stories of transformed coaches and athletes.
* Develop donor newsletters, impact reports, fundraising appeals, and stewardship communications.
* Help communicate the connection between financial partnership and ministry impact.
* Gather stories, testimonies, photos, and statistics that demonstrate FCA's impact.
* Collaborate with marketing/social media efforts to create a consistent development message.

6\. Development Systems \& Administration

* Maintain accurate donor records and relationship information in Aurora FCA's CRM.
* Develop and maintain a donor pipeline.
* Track prospects, meetings, asks, gifts, pledges, and follow\-up.
* Monitor key development metrics including: Total giving, New donors, Donor retention, Recurring donors, Major donor growth, Church partners, Business/community partners, Average gift, Staff fundraising progress
* Ensure timely gift acknowledgement and donor stewardship.
* Develop repeatable systems and processes for fundraising as Aurora FCA grows.

What Success Looks Like

Within the first 12 months, the Development Director will:

* Establish a clear annual development strategy and fundraising calendar.
* Build a healthy pipeline of prospective donors and ministry partners.
* Increase donor retention and recurring giving.
* Develop stronger relationships with key individual donors.
* Establish new church and business partnerships.
* Lead successful year\-end and special fundraising campaigns.
* Equip the board to become more effective ambassadors and fundraisers.
* Create a consistent donor communication and stewardship process.
* Help Aurora FCA move toward greater financial sustainability.
* Develop systems that allow the organization to grow without development becoming dependent on one individual.

new_jobs.title: Managing Director - Central
new_jobs.description:
**About Advanced Energy United**  

Advanced Energy United is a national industry association representing businesses that provide the full range of advanced energy and transportation solutions. Our team works to educate, advocate, and activate in decisionmaker venues across the country.  

We advocate for public policies that enable competition and work alongside our member companies to create economic opportunity, lower consumer costs, and bolster energy reliability and resilience across the country. We work with decision makers at every level of government as well as regulators of energy markets to build progress toward an economy built on advanced energy.  

If you’re an entrepreneurial, innovative, analytical and thoughtful person looking to make an impact in the clean energy space, United might be the perfect place for you to share your talents. Team members at United are given the trust and responsibility to make big things happen, and myriad opportunities to learn new skills, explore new issue areas, and work with a broad cross section of the clean energy community. Being a team member at United also means working with a talented and diverse group of people, some who bring decades of experience spanning advocacy, philanthropy, clean tech, government and more—and our collaborative approach means we get to learn from each other, expert and novice, every day. And while our organization is fully remote, we are proud of the people\-focused culture we have built and the connectedness of our team.  

We work on serious issues, take our mission seriously, but never take ourselves too seriously. **Position Description**  

Advanced Energy United seeks a solutions\-oriented, innovative, and politically savvy Managing Director to join United’s policy team. The Managing Director will oversee a team of advocates and shape policy advocacy strategies in the Central U.S. region, lead member engagement in the region, and work collaboratively with program directors to develop and implement multi\-year strategies and campaigns designed to achieve policy successes that will accelerate the transition to 100% clean energy and electrified transportation while expanding markets for the advanced energy industry.  

This is a unique opportunity to join a high\-functioning team and organization, and lead strategy and execution in key states. The ideal candidate will be a highly energetic and self\-starting professional who brings a background in issue advocacy at the state or federal level and experience with clean energy. The Managing Director will work collaboratively with United’s other Managing Directors, and will lead strategy development and execution, with project teams on both internal and external projects to advance United’s policy agenda in priority states including Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, Texas and Wisconsin. Candidates should be creative and flexible, with the ability to develop and execute strategies, working in multiple venues with diverse stakeholders. The successful candidate will have excellent organizational, managerial and mentoring skills, the ability to find common ground both with corporate membership and external stakeholders, and a successful track record generating revenue. Candidates will need to travel frequently to meet with United members, coalition allies and stakeholders, public officials, and internal team members.

 **Responsibilities**  

* Lead development of political and policy strategies for accelerating the transition to 100% clean energy and electrified transportation, as well as identify future venues for policy and political success in targeted states.
* Manage a geographically dispersed advocacy team and lobbyists on the ground.
* Work collaboratively across United’s policy team on developing and implementing strategies to meet short and long\-term policy objectives in key states as part of United’s core portfolio. This will include legislative, regulatory, and administrative (e.g. governor’s office) engagement.
* Work with United members to develop and reach consensus on policy positions in key states and on key issues. Facilitate member calls and lead policy discussions to coalesce member input and prioritize areas of interest and engagement.
* Work with team members to ensure high\-quality member engagement opportunities are conducted in targeted states through direct decision maker engagement, including lobby days and candidate education, earned media, and expert testimony; and participate in legislative, rulemaking, and administrative processes, as needed.
* Develop and maintain excellent working relationships with coalition partners, philanthropy, allies, and key legislative, regulatory and administrative staff.
* Represent United effectively in front of funders and member prospects and help raise funds to support strategies and engagement in key states.
* Ability to master the politics of the region through development of relationships with key players and decision makers, as well as a general understanding of the levers of power in these states and how to leverage the advanced energy industry to affect policy change.
* Travel on an as needed basis (up to 30%) to targeted states for advocacy days, conferences, meetings with key allies and stakeholders, staff development, and other efforts on behalf of United.

 **Required Qualifications**  

* Bachelor’s and/or Advanced degree, Political Science, Public Policy, or Economics preferred, or applicable comparable experience
* Minimum of ten years of professional experience in public policy, with a portion of that engagement in the clean energy or transportation sector
* Experience managing a team in a remote environment
* Viewed as a subject matter expert in a specific focus area
* Political campaign or organizing experience, preferably in the clean energy advocacy space
* Entrepreneurial approach, flexible attitude, and ability to operate independently, making decisions consistent with United’s mission/v

**Overview**  

The Regional Managing Director, Data Center Community is an externally facing leadership role responsible for earning and sustaining trust in a major Microsoft data center community or regional cluster of communities. The role serves as Microsoft’s local community leader, local stakeholder point of contact, and chief spokesperson for the assigned region, representing the company with civic leaders, elected officials, business organizations, education and workforce partners, nonprofits, media, and community stakeholders.

  

This position is designed for a high\-visibility data center environment where local trust, transparent communications, public engagement, and community benefit are central to Microsoft’s long\-term license to operate. The Managing Director leads a regional team that includes a Community Manager and a Communications Manager and works in close partnership with the local data center operations, as well as Microsoft legal, government affairs, philanthropic and communications teams to deliver a coordinated, locally empowered, and campaign\-ready approach.

  

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

 **Role Scope and Leadership Model**

* Lead Microsoft’s regional data center community strategy, including local stakeholder engagement, public narrative, community investment, and trust\-building priorities.
* Serve as the chief local spokesperson for the region, shaping Microsoft’s voice in community forums, public events, local media engagements, business and civic convenings, and high\-stakes community conversations.
* Manage and guide a regional team and budget consisting of a Community Manager and a Communications Manager, setting priorities, aligning execution, and ensuring the team operates as one integrated local function.
* Partner closely with the local data center operations leader to align community engagement, communications, and operational priorities, ensuring Microsoft shows up as a coordinated and accountable neighbor.
* Coordinate with regional and national surge teams when new market entry, permitting, zoning, local controversy, media attention, or urgent community concerns require additional support.
* Manage a locally focused budget to enable local partnerships and support community priorities in relation to the data center and its operations.
 **Responsibilities** **Regional Leadership and Community Strategy**

* Own and accountable for the integrated community engagement strategy for the assigned data center region, translating Microsoft’s public Community\-First AI Infrastructure commitments into locally relevant plans, partnerships, communications, and measurable outcomes.
* Build and sustain trusted relationships with local elected officials, civic leaders, business organizations, education and workforce institutions, nonprofits, labor partners, community advocates, and other priority stakeholders.
* Represent Microsoft as a trusted local leader in public forums, community meetings, advisory boards, chambers of commerce, business councils, nonprofit coalitions, and other high\-impact venues.
* Anticipate community risks and opportunities, maintain a clear stakeholder map, identify emerging sentiment, and escalate issues quickly with recommendations for action.
* Ensure community engagement begins early, remains transparent, and continues through the full data center lifecycle, including planning, construction, operations, expansion, and moments of heightened scrutiny.
 **Chief Spokesperson and Public Narrative**

* Serve as Microsoft’s chief local spokesperson for the assigned data center community, delivering clear, credible, plain\-language messages about Microsoft’s investments, operations, community commitments and impact, and long\-term presence.
* Guide the local narrative across community engagement, media, social sentiment, public meetings, and stakeholder communications, ensuring consistency with Microsoft’s regional and national messaging while remaining responsive to local needs.
* Prepare for and lead public\-facing engagements such as town halls, hearings, office hours, tours, groundbreaking events, listening sessions, briefings, and community benefit discussions.
* Work with the Communications Manager to develop talking points, FAQs, briefings, local proof points, media materials, rapid\-response guidance, and storytelling that demonstrates Microsoft’s accountability and community impact.
* Act as the trusted local voice during sensitive moments, helping Microsoft respond with transparency, empathy, speed, and operational accuracy.
 **Communications and Community Engagement Oversight**

* Lead the regional team’s budget communications and community engagement operating rhythm, ensuring the Community Manager and Communications Manager have clear priorities, coordinated plans, and defined accountability.
* Oversee local communications strategy, including proactive storytelling, local media engagement, social sentiment monitoring, stakeholder updates, community event messaging, and crisis\-response readiness.
* Guide community programming and philanthropic investments, ensuring local grants, sponsorships, employee engagement, AI skilling, workforce initiatives, nonprofit partnerships, and education programs align with community priorities and Microsoft commitments.
* Connect communications, media, and community efforts so local programs generate credible proof points and community voices that strengthen trust and demonstrate tangible benefit.
* Ensure the regional team maintains accurate data, metrics, outcomes, and qualitative feedback to support internal reporting, public transparency,
